turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's think about it this way: if you were moving a physical object in real life, would shifting it to the right by 3 units still be considered a translation up by 3 units?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess that makes sense. If I move something to the right, it doesn't go up at all. So, does that mean \(f(x-3)\) actually shifts the graph to the right by 3 units instead of up? But then, what does it mean when we say it’s a translation?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Think about it like this: when you move an object to the right in real life, does it actually go up in height at all? Would your method still give the right answer if you were working with physical objects you can see and touch?
